meta.description: Display a paginated list of credit card transactions from the TRANSACT file, allowing users to browse and select individual transactions for detailed viewing.
meta.process_description: This program presents a scrollable, paginated transaction list screen (up to 10 transactions per page) to bank staff or cardholders, reading records from the TRANSACT file sequentially. Users can navigate forward (PF8) and backward (PF7) through pages of transactions, or enter a specific Transaction ID to start browsing from that point. When a user selects a transaction by entering 'S' next to it, the program transfers control to COTRN01C to display the full transaction detail. The program maintains page state (first/last transaction ID on current page, page number, next-page availability flag) in the communication area to support bidirectional pagination across CICS interactions.

files.TRANSACT: Master transaction file containing credit card transaction records (transaction ID, amount, date, and other transaction details) that are browsed sequentially to populate the list screen

business_rules: A maximum of 10 transactions are displayed per page; the program reads exactly 10 records forward or backward from the current browse position.
Only the selection value 'S' (uppercase or lowercase) is valid when selecting a transaction; any other value results in an error message 'Invalid selection. Valid value is S'.
A Transaction ID used as a search/start key must be numeric; non-numeric input is rejected with the message 'Tran ID must be Numeric'.
Forward navigation (PF8) is blocked when already on the last page of transactions, displaying 'You are already at the bottom of the page'.
Backward navigation (PF7) is blocked when already on the first page (page number not greater than 1), displaying 'You are already at the top of the page'.
If no communication area is present (EIBCALEN = 0), the user is redirected to the sign-on screen (COSGN00C), enforcing authenticated access.
Selecting a transaction (flag 'S') causes an immediate transfer of control (XCTL) to COTRN01C for transaction detail viewing, passing the selected transaction ID via the communication area.
PF3 returns the user to the main menu program (COMEN01C), providing standard navigation back to the application menu.

The program preserves the first and last transaction IDs of the current page in the communication area to enable accurate bidirectional pagination across multiple CICS pseudo-conversational interactions.

Advances the transaction list to the next page by reading up to 10 transactions forward from the current position in the transaction master file. It updates the page counter, determines whether further pages exist, and refreshes the screen with the new set of transactions.
Opens a sequential browse of the transaction master file starting from the last transaction ID visible on the current page, establishing the forward read position.

variables.name: WS-VARIABLES
variables.description: Top-level working storage group containing all operational variables used by the Transaction List program during its execution cycle.

variables.name: WS-PGMNAME
variables.description: The internal name of this program (COTRN00C), used when transferring control to other programs or logging errors so the system knows which program initiated the action.

variables.name: WS-TRANID
variables.description: The CICS transaction identifier (CT00) associated with the Transaction List screen. This is the 4-character code a user or the system uses to invoke the transaction list function within the CardDemo application.

variables.name: WS-MESSAGE
variables.description: The feedback message displayed to the user at the bottom of the transaction list screen. Contains informational or error messages such as 'Invalid selection. Valid value is S' or 'You are already at the bottom of the page' to guide user navigation and correct data entry.

variables.name: WS-TRANSACT-FILE
variables.description: The name of the master transaction file (TRANSACT) that stores all credit card transaction records. This value is used when opening, browsing, and closing the file to retrieve transactions for display on the list screen.

variables.name: WS-ERR-FLG
variables.description: An error indicator that tracks whether a business or validation error has occurred during the current user interaction (e.g., invalid selection value, non-numeric transaction ID). When set to 'Y', the program suppresses navigation and redisplays the screen with an appropriate error message.

variables.name: ERR-FLG-ON
variables.description: Condition name indicating that an error has been detected during the current interaction, such as an invalid transaction selection or non-numeric search input. When true, the program will display an error message and prevent further navigation.

variables.name: ERR-FLG-OFF
variables.description: Condition name indicating that no errors have been detected during the current interaction. When true, the program proceeds normally with pagination or transaction selection.

variables.name: WS-TRANSACT-EOF
variables.description: End-of-file indicator for the TRANSACT file browse operation. Signals that the program has reached the last available transaction record while reading forward through the file, which determines whether a next page of transactions exists and controls the availability of the forward navigation (PF8) key.

variables.name: TRANSACT-EOF
variables.description: Condition name indicating that all available transaction records have been read from the TRANSACT file. When true, the program knows there are no more transactions beyond the current page, blocking forward pagination and informing the user they are at the last page.

variables.name: TRANSACT-NOT-EOF
variables.description: Condition name indicating that more transaction records exist beyond those currently read from the TRANSACT file. When true, the program allows the user to navigate forward to the next page of transactions.

variables.name: WS-SEND-ERASE-FLG
variables.description: Controls how the transaction list screen is refreshed when sent to the user's terminal. When set to 'Y', the entire screen is erased and rewritten (full refresh), typically on first display. When 'N', only changed fields are updated, providing a smoother navigation experience during pagination.

variables.name: SEND-ERASE-YES
variables.description: Condition name indicating the transaction list screen should be fully erased and redrawn on the next send operation. Used on initial display or after significant screen state changes.

variables.name: SEND-ERASE-NO
variables.description: Condition name indicating the transaction list screen should be partially updated rather than fully redrawn, used during normal pagination to update only the transaction rows and navigation fields.

variables.name: WS-RESP-CD
variables.description: The CICS response code returned after each file or system operation (e.g., reading the TRANSACT file). Used to detect whether an operation succeeded or encountered an error such as a record not found or end of file, enabling appropriate error handling.

variables.name: WS-REAS-CD
variables.description: The CICS reason code providing additional detail about the outcome of a file or system operation. Used alongside WS-RESP-CD to diagnose specific error conditions when reading the TRANSACT file or performing other CICS commands.

variables.name: WS-REC-COUNT
variables.description: A running count of how many transaction records have been read and placed on the current page during a browse operation. Ensures that exactly up to 10 transactions are displayed per page, controlling when the page population loop stops.

variables.name: WS-IDX
variables.description: A loop index that tracks which of the 10 transaction row slots on the screen is currently being populated. Increments with each transaction record read, ensuring each transaction is placed in the correct display row on the list screen.

variables.name: WS-PAGE-NUM
variables.description: A working storage page counter used internally during the page population logic to track and update the current page number. After page loading is complete, this value is stored in the communication area so the user sees the correct page number on screen.

variables.name: WS-TRAN-AMT
variables.description: The formatted monetary amount of a transaction, displayed on the transaction list screen. The format includes a sign indicator and two decimal places, allowing users to see both credit and debit transaction amounts clearly (e.g., +00001234.56 or -00000050.00).

variables.name: WS-TRAN-DATE
variables.description: The formatted date of a transaction displayed on the transaction list screen in MM/DD/YY format. Allows users to quickly identify when each transaction occurred while browsing the list.

variables.name: CDEMO-CT00-INFO
variables.description: A group of fields specific to the Transaction List screen (CT00) that are preserved across pseudo-conversational interactions. These fields maintain pagination state, user selection, and navigation context between each user action and the program's next execution.

variables.name: CDEMO-CT00-TRNID-FIRST
variables.description: The transaction ID of the first transaction displayed on the current page. Stored in the communication area between interactions so that when the user presses PF7 (page backward), the program knows where to start reading backwards through the TRANSACT file to reconstruct the previous page.

variables.name: CDEMO-CT00-TRNID-LAST
variables.description: The transaction ID of the last transaction displayed on the current page. Stored in the communication area between interactions so that when the user presses PF8 (page forward), the program knows where to resume reading forward through the TRANSACT file to load the next page.

variables.name: CDEMO-CT00-PAGE-NUM
variables.description: The current page number shown to the user on the transaction list screen. Persisted in the communication area between interactions so the program can increment or decrement it correctly during forward or backward navigation, and block backward navigation when already on page 1.

variables.name: CDEMO-CT00-NEXT-PAGE-FLG
variables.description: An indicator stored between interactions that records whether more transactions exist beyond the current page. When 'Y', the user is allowed to press PF8 to navigate forward. When 'N', forward navigation is blocked and the user is informed they are at the last page of transactions.

variables.name: NEXT-PAGE-YES
variables.description: Condition name indicating that additional transaction records exist beyond the current page, enabling the user to press PF8 to navigate forward to the next page of transactions.

variables.name: NEXT-PAGE-NO
variables.description: Condition name indicating that no further transaction records exist beyond the current page. When true, the program blocks forward navigation and displays the message 'You are already at the bottom of the page'.

variables.name: CDEMO-CT00-TRN-SEL-FLG
variables.description: The selection flag entered by the user next to a transaction row on the list screen. The only valid business value is 'S' (or 's'), which signals the user's intent to view the full details of that transaction. Any other value triggers a validation error message.

variables.name: CDEMO-CT00-TRN-SELECTED
variables.description: The transaction ID of the specific transaction the user has chosen to view in detail. When the user selects a transaction with 'S', this field is populated and passed via the communication area to the Transaction Detail program (COTRN01C), which uses it to retrieve and display the full transaction record.

variables.name: DFHCOMMAREA
variables.description: The CICS communication area passed between program invocations in the pseudo-conversational interaction model. Carries state information (pagination anchors, page number, user selection, navigation flags) from one execution of the Transaction List program to the next, enabling the program to resume exactly where the user left off.

variables.name: LK-COMMAREA
variables.description: The linkage section placeholder for the CICS communication area data passed between program executions. Its presence (checked via EIBCALEN > 0) confirms that the user has already been authenticated and the program is being re-entered; its absence triggers a redirect to the sign-on screen (COSGN00C) to enforce security.

paragraphs.name: MAIN-PARA
paragraphs.description: MAIN-PARA is the central orchestration entry point of the transaction list program. It enforces authenticated access, determines whether the user is arriving for the first time or returning after an action, and routes each user interaction (navigation, selection, or menu return) to the appropriate business process before suspending and awaiting the next user input.

paragraphs.name: PROCESS-ENTER-KEY
paragraphs.description: This paragraph processes the Enter key action on the transaction list screen, identifying which transaction row the user has selected, validating the selection and any manually entered Transaction ID search key, then either transferring control to the transaction detail program or refreshing the list from the beginning of the matching page.

paragraphs.name: PROCESS-PF7-KEY
paragraphs.description: Handles the user's request to navigate backward to the previous page of transactions. It validates whether a previous page exists and either scrolls back one page or informs the user they are already at the beginning of the transaction list.

paragraphs.name: PROCESS-PF8-KEY
paragraphs.description: Handles the user's request to navigate forward to the next page of transactions. It either advances to the next page of results or informs the user they have already reached the last available page.

paragraphs.name: PROCESS-PAGE-FORWARD
paragraphs.description: Advances the transaction list to the next page by reading up to 10 transactions forward from the current position in the transaction master file. It updates the page counter, determines whether further pages exist, and refreshes the screen with the new set of transactions.

paragraphs.name: PROCESS-PAGE-BACKWARD
paragraphs.description: This paragraph handles backward pagination through the transaction list, rebuilding the previous page of up to 10 transactions by reading the TRANSACT file in reverse from the current position. It updates the displayed page number and refreshes the screen so the user can review earlier transactions.

paragraphs.name: POPULATE-TRAN-DATA
paragraphs.description: This paragraph formats and loads a single transaction record's details into the correct row slot on the paginated transaction list screen. It also tracks the first and last transaction IDs on the page to enable accurate forward and backward navigation across screen interactions.

paragraphs.name: INITIALIZE-TRAN-DATA
paragraphs.description: Clears the display fields for a specific transaction row on the list screen, based on which row position (1–10) is currently being processed. This ensures that any row not populated with a real transaction record appears blank rather than showing stale or residual data from a previous screen refresh.

paragraphs.name: RETURN-TO-PREV-SCREEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph handles the exit navigation from the transaction list screen, transferring control back to the appropriate previous screen — defaulting to the sign-on screen if no prior destination was recorded. It ensures the communication area is correctly stamped with the current program's identity before handing off control.

paragraphs.name: SEND-TRNLST-SCREEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph renders the transaction list screen to the bank staff or cardholder, displaying up to 10 paginated credit card transactions along with any relevant status or error messages. It determines whether to fully repaint the screen or perform a lighter refresh based on the current display state.

paragraphs.name: RECEIVE-TRNLST-SCREEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph captures the user's input from the transaction list screen, collecting any navigation requests, search criteria, or transaction selections that the bank staff or cardholder has entered before the program processes their intended action.

paragraphs.name: POPULATE-HEADER-INFO
paragraphs.description: Populates the standard screen header area with application branding, current date, and current time before displaying the transaction list to the user. This ensures every screen presented to bank staff or cardholders carries consistent identification information and an accurate timestamp for audit and usability purposes.

paragraphs.name: STARTBR-TRANSACT-FILE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph initiates a sequential browse of the transaction master file starting from a specific Transaction ID entered by the user or held from the previous page. It handles cases where the requested starting transaction is not found or the file is unavailable, ensuring the user receives appropriate feedback before any records are displayed.

paragraphs.name: READNEXT-TRANSACT-FILE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph retrieves the next sequential transaction record from the master transaction file during a forward page browse operation. It handles three outcomes: successful record retrieval, end of available transactions, or an unexpected system error.

paragraphs.name: READPREV-TRANSACT-FILE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph retrieves the previous transaction record from the master transaction file, enabling backward pagination through the transaction list. It handles the case where the beginning of the file has been reached, as well as any unexpected file access errors, ensuring the user receives appropriate feedback in either situation.

paragraphs.name: ENDBR-TRANSACT-FILE
paragraphs.description: Closes the sequential browse session against the transaction master file once the current page of transactions has been fully read. This is a necessary housekeeping step that releases the file browse cursor held by the system, ensuring no file resources are left open between user interactions.
